subject: Mid-quarter course-correct: OKR scopes, priority shifts, and dependency asks
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@boardmail.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:32:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-quarter course-correct: OKR scopes, priority shifts, and dependency asks

Team —

Quick mid-quarter check. Running a short pulse across leadership before the QBR next week. I reviewed current progress against our Q3 OKRs and recommend three targeted scope adjustments to keep the most customer-impacting work on track. High-level summary first, details + asks below.

Summary:
- Keep latency/throughput initiative (OBJ-1) prioritized — failing this hurts renewals for two key customers.
- Re-scope the experimental multi-model routing work to a slim MVP (feature flag + limited models) and move the broader rollout to Q4 (OBJ-2).
- Postpone noncritical UX polish for the Console until after QBR; shift those EEs to support infra/dependency work.

Dependency asks (what I need from each of you by EOD Wednesday):
- Vivek: Can SRE allocate 1.5 FTEs for two sprints to unblock cross-region KV cache replication? This is the gating item for latency improvements. See sheet attached.
- Lauren: Product OKR owners: please finalize the reduced MVP scope for multi-model routing (<=3 user flows) and a canary plan. I need the scope doc so I can sign off on Thursday.
- Marcus: Engineering manager ask — confirm whether the two backend ICs we planned to rotate onto Console polish can be pulled for dependency work instead. If not, propose alternatives.
- Dylan: Can you consolidate the customer-impact tickets (Priority P0/P1) into a single triage board and share a short runbook for execs?

Attachments: QBR_prep_deck_v1.pdf (draft slides), dependency-triage-sheet.xlsx (current blockers + owners).

Goal for this thread: agree on the re-scope and resource moves so I can update execs and the board (Tom is cc'd) with a clear, mitigated plan.

Thanks —
Monica
Monica Patel
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter course-correct: OKR scopes, priority shifts, and dependency asks

Monica —

Thanks for the crisp summary. Quick responses inline: 

- SRE capacity: I can allocate 1 FTE immediately and a second for one sprint starting Aug 3. We have a hiring freeze on new contractors this quarter, so the 1.5FTE ask will be a mix of reassigning an on-call rotation and a temporary focus shift. I'll confirm the exact engineers by Wed EOD.

- KV replication work: the timeline looks tight if we pursue cross-region consistency plus incremental rollout. Proposal: prioritize read-path KV cache invalidation and asynchronous replication first — that buys most latency wins without full-consistency complexity.

- Risks: shifting two backend ICs off Console will delay a small set of UX fixes that our CS team flagged. If we reassign, we should add a customer-facing communication plan.

I'll update the dependency-triage-sheet with engineers assigned and a short mitigation note.

—Vivek
VP, Infrastructure and Reliability

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter course-correct: OKR scopes, priority shifts, and dependency asks

Monica / team —

I ran a quick triage with PMs this morning and here are concrete outputs for the reduced MVP for multi-model routing: 

MVP scope (to ship in 6 weeks):
- Support model selection via policy with up to 3 models (fallback chain).
- API flagging and telemetry for experiments (no UI for model selection in V1).
- Canary rules scoped to 10% of traffic for two customer cohorts.

Out-of-scope for Q3 (moved to Q4):
- UI-driven model picker, full routing rules editor, dynamic model composition.

Canary plan: product will own rollout controls; infra will provide the routing layer + KV cache changes. I will drop the MVP scope doc and a one-page rollback plan in the shared drive by 16:00 Wed.

On resources: Marcus, we should be able to repurpose one backend IC for the next two sprints. If you can free up another engineer (even part-time), we can avoid hitting the CS backlog hard.

- Lauren
Head of Product

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@boardmail.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-quarter course-correct: OKR scopes, priority shifts, and dependency asks

Thanks all — quick decisions and next steps: 

1) Scope: We align on the reduced multi-model routing MVP Lauren outlined. Q3 will surface significant customer value and keeps the broader UX work for Q4.

2) Infra: Vivek — proceed with the asymmetric replication approach (read-path + async replication) as the path to hit our latency SLOs. Confirm the specific engineers in the triage sheet by Wed EOD; I'll sign off on the temporary reallocation when I see names.

3) Resources: Marcus — please reassign 1 backend IC full-time and 1 partial (30%) for two sprints. If that's impossible, propose alternate names by Wed noon.

4) CS & comms: Dylan — draft a short customer note for the affected cohorts and the CS playbook for any rollback. Put it in the shared drive and ping me when it's ready.

5) QBR: I'll incorporate these scope adjustments and the risk mitigation slides into the deck. Tom — I'm keeping you looped for board context; we'll share the final QBR deck on Friday.

I'll update the Drive folder and attach the next deck iteration once I incorporate the triage inputs. Appreciate the quick responses — this is the right minimal-risk path to hit our key outcomes.

Monica
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
